content.text: The issue branch creates Server objects that:
1. Load xml bean definitions from FEDORA_HOME/server/config/spring
2. Translates the fcfg module definitions into bean definitions
There is some weirdness about relative pathing of the resource index data that I'm working on.
Update on the issue branch:
Servers create a Spring application context, and register themselves as a singleton bean.  Servers create a child context for all other beans, including modules.
Servers register bean definitions from ${fedora.home}/server/config/spring with an XML bean definition reader
Servers parse the fcfg, and create bean definitions from all module configurations.
Server required module roles are validated if they appear as Spring bean definitions or ar fcfg configurations.
Servers instantiate all modules as Spring beans.  This allows all the modules, and the context Server, to be autowired into other Spring bean definitions.
Existing modules can run un-changed; most Spring work confined to the Server abstract class.  ResourceIndex modifed to allow location of triplestore connector via Spring.
Outstanding concerns:
1. Ensure the Server.overrideModuleClass and Server.overrideModuleRole methods work as intended when object definitions are loaded as Spring beans
2. Identify global fcfg values and implement GlobalConfig
3. Identify references to ServerConfiguration that can be replaced with getters or bean definition refs in 3.5

Should the override-able ModelBasedTripleGenerator configuration be moved out of code in Server, and into a default Spring xml file in the config directory?  There is a dependency between ResourceIndex and TripleGenerator, so maybe the in-code definition could check first whether there is a local bean definition.
Moving out of 3.4 and into 3.5, lack of time to complete implementation for 3.4
initial
move has been made
Use standard, well-known frameworks/libraries to:
Resolve inter-module dependencies via dependency injection
Provide hooks to initialize/de-initialize modules when the webapp container starts and stops
Allow re-configuration and plugging in of alternative modules without re-compiling
For more in-depth information on this work, please see:
http://fedora-commons.org/confluence/x/JAAbAQ

1. Load xml bean definitions from FEDORA_HOME/server/config/spring
2. Translates the fcfg module definitions into bean definitions

There is some weirdness about relative pathing of the resource index data that I'm working on.

Update on the issue branch:

  • Servers create a Spring application context, and register themselves as a singleton bean. Servers create a child context for all other beans, including modules.
  • Servers register bean definitions from $ {fedora.home}

    /server/config/spring with an XML bean definition reader

  • Servers parse the fcfg, and create bean definitions from all module configurations.
  • Server required module roles are validated if they appear as Spring bean definitions or ar fcfg configurations.
  • Servers instantiate all modules as Spring beans. This allows all the modules, and the context Server, to be autowired into other Spring bean definitions.
  • Existing modules can run un-changed; most Spring work confined to the Server abstract class. ResourceIndex modifed to allow location of triplestore connector via Spring.

Outstanding concerns:
1. Ensure the Server.overrideModuleClass and Server.overrideModuleRole methods work as intended when object definitions are loaded as Spring beans
2. Identify global fcfg values and implement GlobalConfig
3. Identify references to ServerConfiguration that can be replaced with getters or bean definition refs in 3.5

Should the override-able ModelBasedTripleGenerator configuration be moved out of code in Server, and into a default Spring xml file in the config directory? There is a dependency between ResourceIndex and TripleGenerator, so maybe the in-code definition could check first whether there is a local bean definition.

Use standard, well-known frameworks/libraries to:

  • Resolve inter-module dependencies via dependency injection
  • Provide hooks to initialize/de-initialize modules when the webapp container starts and stops
  • Allow re-configuration and plugging in of alternative modules without re-compiling

For more in-depth information on this work, please see: http://fedora-commons.org/confluence/x/JAAbAQ
